pattern.chosen_from: generated grammar: 22 cell types x (1, 447) cells, optional intro/outro/coda, roster 20 of 22 functions

meter.chosen_from: 178 derived cycles (beats envelope [2, 12], slots envelope [5, 48]), measured BY DERIVATION ON THE DECLARED COORDINATE: 1 of 11 beats-per-line values, then 1 of 15 bars x subdivision factorisation(s) of 12 beats, then 1 of 12 groupings of 12. The line runs 12 beat(s) — at most the density band's ceiling, since a sung line carries at least one syllable a beat — and holds 24 slot(s), at least the band's floor. Both ends are the same calibrated band in different units; the pair share follows from how many ways each beat count factorises. Unit is notation, never enforced

placements.measure: uniform per MEMBER over the pool; per member and not per group because 8 of the 77 registered schemas anchor one member at each end of a word
placements.token_ceiling_from: the smaller of the floor's measured tokens-per-line floor 7.25 and this plan's own shortest line (12 syllable(s) after its pickup) less one for the last word — a plan asks for the n-th word only where BOTH the calibration and this meter say a line carries that many

density.chosen_from: uniform over 1..4 per PLAN (the line-binding ceiling), from a stream seeded on (seed, 'density'); each line then draws its participation uniform over 1..2, and the end-rhyme pass binds free line ends on top (M-191)

end_rhyme.chosen_from: NOT A DRAW — each sung section's own `schemes[fn].rgs` re-realised at the line ends, so this consumes no seed entropy and the placement draw above is untouched. Three counts, never summed (doctrine 79): `added` groups emitted; `blocked` blocks whose ends the placement draw had already spent; `narrow` blocks whose lines cannot carry one more DISTINCT word.

relations.chosen_from: uniform per group over the bare default plus the 22 certified drawable schemas (relations.DRAWABLE_SCHEMAS, witness-certified — M-117). The bare default lands on 1 draw in 23, a rarity this disclosure exists to hand the owner, exactly as the placement draw's `end` share was. A group binding declared tokens draws only from the schemas the pair route can bind there (relations.pair_bindable, M-149a); the rest stay drawable at default slots

narrative.chosen_from: uniform over the 257472 legal story line-ups of this shape (quality/narrative.py, M-121; the count is exact and the draw is entropy-last)

writer_brief:
Write a song: 22 lines, 8 sections, in this order:
  [VAMP — 3 lines — 3 bars of 12/8, one-beat pickup]
      up to 12 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [PRECHORUS — 1 line — 1 bar of 12/8]
      up to 12 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [CHORUS — 3 lines — 3 bars of 12/8]
      up to 12 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [CHORUS — 3 lines — 3 bars of 12/8]
      up to 12 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [POSTCHORUS — 5 lines — 5 bars of 12/8, half-beat pickup]
      up to 12 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [VERSE — 4 lines — 4 bars of 12/8]
      up to 12 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [BRIDGE — 1 line — 1 bar of 12/8, half-beat pickup]
      up to 12 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
  [CODA — 2 lines — 2 bars of 12/8]
      up to 12 syllables a line after the pickup; the calibrated band asks at least 5
Feel: 12/8 grouped 3+2+2+3+2.
Rhyme plan (line numbers over the whole song):
  lines 1.T7 & 2.T3 & 3.T7 stand in internal rhyme — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 6.T7 & 7.T7 stand in family rhyme — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 5 & 7.T2 stand in analysed rhyme — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 11.T6 & 12.T2 & 15.T6 stand in perfect rhyme — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 12.T6 & 14.head stand in pantun ABAB — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 13.T2 & 15.head stand in internal rhyme — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 16.T7 & 17.T2 & 19.T5 stand in consonance — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 16.T5 & 18.T2 & 19.head stand in anaphora — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 21.T7 & 22.T5 stand in pararhyme — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 21.T2 & 22 stand in cluster consonance / skothending span — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 1 & 2 & 3 stand in pantun ABAB — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 6 & 7 stand in light rhyme — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 11 & 12 & 15 stand in monorhyme / leash — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
  lines 16 & 17 & 19 stand in cluster consonance / skothending span — a NAMED relation, judged as itself, not as plain rhyme
Story plan (one job per sung section; each enters from the section before it as stated):
  VAMP1 holds the moment and deepens it, without advancing
  PRECHORUS1 holds the moment and deepens it, without advancing — set beside (connection unstated) VAMP1
  CHORUS1 is the fixed claim the song keeps returning to — set beside (connection unstated) PRECHORUS1
  CHORUS2 is the fixed claim the song keeps returning to — because of CHORUS1
  POSTCHORUS1 is a compressed verdict on what has happened — after CHORUS2
  VERSE1 lets the pressure in — because of POSTCHORUS1
  BRIDGE1 flips the reading of everything before it — against VERSE1
  CODA1 is the leave-taking — the walk home — because of BRIDGE1
Every chorus after the first repeats the first chorus word for word, line for line.
Line 5 is the hook — make it the line someone leaves humming.
Where a binding sits (a bare line number is its end word, read as a rhyme span):
  T7: word 7, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  T3: word 3, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  T2: word 2, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  T6: word 6, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
  head: the first word, its first syllable — the head-rhyme / alliteration reading
  T5: word 5, read as a rhyme span — from its last stressed syllable to its end
What each named relation asks of the bound words:
  internal rhyme: the bound words agree on nucleus, coda; different words, judged inside the line — NOT heard as end rhyme
  family rhyme: the bound words agree on nucleus; coda agree by CLASS, not sound (declared manner partition); different words, judged at the line end — NOT heard as end rhyme
  analysed rhyme: the bound words agree on nucleus; differ on coda; different words, judged at the line end — NOT heard as end rhyme
  perfect rhyme (also: full rhyme): the bound words agree on nucleus, coda, onset (after the stressed syllable), prominence; differ on onset (at the stressed syllable); neither word runs on past the rhyme; different words, judged at the line end
  pantun ABAB: the bound words agree on nucleus, coda; different words, judged at the line end
  consonance: the bound words agree on coda; differ on nucleus; different words, judged at the line end — NOT heard as end rhyme
  anaphora: the bound words agree on token; the same word, judged at the line head — NOT heard as end rhyme
  pararhyme: the bound words agree on onset, coda; differ on nucleus; different words, judged at the line end — NOT heard as end rhyme
  cluster consonance / skothending span: the bound words differ on nucleus; consonants judged by SEQUENCE-AGREE; different words, judged at the line end — NOT heard as end rhyme
  light rhyme (also: anisobaric): the bound words agree on nucleus, coda; differ on prominence; different words, judged at the line end
  monorhyme / leash: the bound words agree on nucleus, coda; different words, judged at the line end
